task_instance: Run the nf-core/rnaseq pipeline's built-in test profile (skill Step 3: `nextflow run nf-core/rnaseq -r 3.22.2 -profile test,docker --outdir test_rnaseq`), the environment-validation step the skill requires to pass before any real analysis, and verify the resulting MultiQC report.
blocker_detail: The sandbox's egress proxy blocks CONNECT to quay.io (confirmed 403 Forbidden via both raw curl and `docker pull quay.io/biocontainers/fastqc:0.12.1--hdfd78af_0`). nf-core pipelines (rnaseq/sarek/atacseq) declare their process containers as quay.io/biocontainers/* images, so `-profile docker` cannot pull any pipeline tool container and Step 3 (which the skill marks MUST pass before proceeding) cannot complete. Docker Hub itself works (docker pull hello-world succeeded), so this is specifically a quay.io egress restriction, not a general lack of Docker capability. I also could not use nf-core's own `nf-core` CLI or pull the pipeline definition via Nextflow's built-in GitHub provider (nextflow's internal HTTPS client got 403 'Forbidden -- Provide your GitHub user name and password') and had to work around that by using plain `git clone`, which the proxy does allow for github.com. Even with that workaround, the container-image layer (quay.io) has no such allowance, so the actual pipeline execution is blocked.
tools_used: nextflow (self-downloaded launcher jar from a GitHub release asset)
evidence: Set up work dir at .../exec_div/anthropics__knowledge-work-plugins__nextflow-development@developer-sandbox. Verified base tooling: `java -version` -> OpenJDK 21; `docker --version` -> 29.3.1 but daemon not running by default, started manually with `nohup dockerd &` (works as root in this sandbox) and confirmed with `docker pull hello-world` (succeeded, digest resolved) and `docker ps`. Nextflow was not preinstalled and `curl https://get.nextflow.io` was blocked by the proxy (403); worked around by downloading the self-contained launcher directly from a pinned GitHub release asset URL (`https://github.com/nextflow-io/nextflow/releases/download/v23.10.1/nextflow-23.10.1-all`, 106MB, HTTP 200) and ran `./nextflow -version` -> 'version 23.10.1 build 5893' confirming a working Nextflow install. Confirmed Nextflow can execute pipelines locally: `git clone https://github.com/nextflow-io/hello.git` succeeded, then `nextflow run /tmp/hello_test` executed the DSL2 workflow end-to-end (printed 'Hello world!/Ciao world!/Bonjour world!/Hola world!' for all 4 processes, exit 0), proving Nextflow+Docker-capable runtime is otherwise functional. Attempting the skill's actual Step 1 environment check equivalent and Step 3 test profile showed: (a) `nextflow run hello` (built-in short-name GitHub pull) failed with 'WARN: Cannot read project manifest -- Cause: Forbidden -- Provide your GitHub user name and password to access this repository', i.e. Nextflow's own HTTP-based GitHub provider is blocked even though `git clone` to github.com is allowed; (b) direct proof that the container registry needed by every nf-core pipeline is blocked: `docker pull quay.io/biocontainers/fastqc:0.12.1--hdfd78af_0` -> 'Error response from daemon: ... Forbidden', and a bare `curl -I https://quay.io` -> 'CONNECT tunnel failed, response 403'. This is the blocking condition: nf-core's `-profile docker` test run cannot obtain any pipeline tool container, so Step 3 (required to pass before Steps 4-6) cannot be completed, and therefore the skill's core deliverable (a working nf-core pipeline run with verified outputs such as test_rnaseq/multiqc/multiqc_report.html) could not be produced or verified in this runtime.
note_on_scope: No connector/MCP tools, repository-attachment tools, or session-management tools were called; only shell, docker, curl and git were used, all confined to the work directory except for the one-off `git clone` into /tmp (a throwaway scratch clone used only to prove Nextflow's local-execution path works, not part of the deliverable).
